items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: I wanted to be a kind of a Hoagy Carmichael sort of guy, or some piano player sitting in the corner kind of telling a story.

ctx.x: I wonder if you can imagine when you were studying English Literature that you were going to be a lyricist who wrote — I’m looking for the correct adjective here — down home lyrics that tell an interesting story.

It’s all due to Mose Allison and Bob Dylan. Those two guys wrote in a way that I really respected. And I never wanted to be a clever writer. I wanted to be a kind of a Hoagy Carmichael sort of guy, or some piano player sitting in the corner kind of telling a story. That’s part of the romance I think of what I thought of as the jazz life early on, being that character. So the — you create your persona. You create your character. I mean I’m exactly who I am when I’m on stage, but I’m focused. It’s not all who I am,…

who I am that I want to communicate in order to tell a particular story. And the lyrics that I’ve come up with over the years and the songs all serve that, which is a lot like, I think, writing a short story where everything is trying to serve not just a punch line or a message but an environment. This is an environment. You know there doesn’t have to be an answer to everything. We can sometimes just paint the picture and let the picture talk for itself. And so that’s kind of how I approach lyric writing; not…
